subject: POC environment options + proposed onramp plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mark Owens <mark.owens@vividhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC environment options + proposed onramp plan

Hi Mark / Vivid team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the trial moving: 

Recap of the three environment options we discussed:
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest to start, no infra for Vivid to manage; good for a first functional evaluation.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, data isolated on Redwood managed capacity.
- VPC trial (Private deployment): customer-managed VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, suitable if data residency / network controls are required.

Proposed success criteria (draft — please adjust):
- Latency P95 <= 200ms for 512-token generation on canonical prompts.
- Throughput: sustain 30 concurrent sessions with per-request tail latency SLA.
- Quality: >92% pass rate on your reference eval set (we'll map your test prompts to expected outputs).
- Cost framing: baseline token cost estimate in the attached trial matrix.

Suggested timeline (typical, can compress):
- Week 0: Environment decision + sign trial MOU (1–2 business days).
- Week 1: Provisioning and network setup (VPC peering / certs / firewall rules) or sandbox provisioning.
- Week 2: Baseline functional validation with seed prompts and test dataset.
- Weeks 3–4: Load/latency testing, quality evals, and handoff to CS for next steps.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood Sales / Deal lead: Ben Carter (me) — overall coordination / purchase questions.
- Redwood Solutions Engineer (onboarding & tests): Marissa Cole — technical onramp, runbook, test harnesses.
- Customer Success: Neha Kapoor — adoption criteria and success metrics.
- Vivid: Mark Owens — systems owner; Procurement to coordinate PO.

Next steps for you: please confirm 1) preferred environment (Hosted | Dedicated sandbox | VPC trial), 2) any hard constraints (KMS/HSM, IP allowlist, SOC 2 evidence needs), and 3) a preferred kickoff window (we have availability next Tue/Thu mornings PT).

Attached: redwood_trial_matrix.xlsx (cost/throughput compare), vivid_po_template.pdf.

If VPC is preferred, Marissa will follow with a short technical checklist and a proposed peering runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0124

Attachments: redwood_trial_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), vivid_po_template.pdf (PDF)

3) Procurement will need your standard PO template (attached on our side).

We can aim for the week of Oct 11 for a kickoff. Please send the peering/runbook and a short checklist for what we need to prepare on our side.

CC'ing procurement to keep them in the loop.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC environment options + proposed onramp plan

Perfect — thanks Mark. VPC it is. Quick operational notes so procurement and your infra team have what they need: 

High-level onramp steps (we'll provide a detailed runbook):
- NDA/DPA and SOC 2 evidence exchange (we'll send standard links; SOC 2 report by secure upload).
- Sign trial MOU + PO (procurement). We received your note — we'll accept your PO template and send back a countersigned MOU.
- Network setup: exchange of IP ranges, peer a VPN or AWS/GCP VPC peering (your preference), and TLS cert exchange.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK) and HSM integrations — Marissa will coordinate implementation details.
- Test data: we recommend starting with a sanitized subset of production prompts; we'll validate on synthetic data until DPA is signed.

Proposed trimmed timeline given VPC:
- Oct 5–7: Legal + procurement paperwork
- Oct 8–11: Network & KMS onboarding (low-friction if we get IPs and IAM roles early)
- Oct 12: 60-min technical kickoff (Marissa + infra)
- Oct 13–20: Functional validation and test harness run
- Oct 21–Nov 3: Load & quality evaluation (final readouts)

Marissa — can you attach the VPC onramp checklist and a short list of exact values/profiles they should prepare? Neha — will pick up the success criteria mapping once we have their test prompts.

Ben

Attachments: (we will upload SOC 2 link and countersigned MOU once legal confirms)

On Mon, Oct 4, 2027 at 10:20 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Perfect — thanks Mark. VPC it is. Quick operational notes so procurement and your infra team have what they need:

Hi Mark — following up with the technical checklist and evaluation plan (high level). I've attached a PDF checklist (redwood_vpc_onramp_checklist.pdf) and included the essentials below so your infra team can triage: 

VPC onramp checklist (minimum):
- CIDR block(s) to peer (please provide both prod and staging ranges if applicable).
- Preferred peering method: AWS VPC peering / Shared VPC / VPN (indicate account IDs).
- Public key(s) / TLS certs for mutual TLS (we can exchange via secure upload).
- IAM role/service account for Redwood egress (if using cloud-native peering).
- KMS customer-managed key ARN(s) or HSM contact details and rotation policy.
- IP allowlist for management plane (we'll provide our egress IPs).
- Expected data types for the trial and whether any will be PHI (for legal/data handling).

Evaluation plan & success mapping (we will instrument metrics and hand over a short report at the end of the trial):
- Functional validation (Marissa): verify canonical prompts, deterministic control prompts, and a small suite of 250 reference prompts from Vivid. Goal: >=92% match on labeled outputs.
- Latency (Marissa + Infra): measure p50/p95/p99 for 256 and 512 token generations under baseline and 30 concurrent connections. Goal: p95 <= 200ms for 512 tokens.
- Throughput (Neha): ramp test to 30 concurrent sessions with 1-min sustained rate. Goal: no request errors >0.5% and controlled queuing/backpressure.
- Cost & unit economics (Ben): we will capture token counts and provide a per-1M token estimate for each environment variant.

Owners & contacts: 
- Ben Carter (AE) — ben.carter@redwood.com — procurement, timeline, pricing
- Marissa Cole (Solutions Eng) — marissa.cole@redwood.com — technical onboarding, test harness
- Neha Kapoor (Customer Success) — neha.kapoor@redwood.com — success criteria and post-trial adoption

Kickoff logistics: please share an install window (Oct 11 works for us) and attach the CIDR/IPs and your preferred peering method. We'll schedule a 60-min kickoff with infra and provide scripted smoke tests to run during the session.

Regards,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_vpc_onramp_checklist.pdf (PDF)
